correctness.rationale: The full three-node half-period propagator has eigenvalues e^{-2 gamma h}, e^{-2 gamma h ±2F(beta h)} and a simple Perron root. The strictly convex F gives unique critical half-period. The Poincaré map is cooperative and strictly subhomogeneous, proving the off-critical global attractor statements. At criticality the positive periodic adjoint gives a strict extinction Lyapunov function for every nonzero trajectory. Projection onto the sole neutral Perron mode gives r_{n+1}=r_n-q r_n^2+o(r_n^2), and therefore n r_n tends to 1/q. Reflection reduces q to the stated elementary formula. Standalone exact symbolic identities and a numerical test replay successfully. No finite experiment substitutes for the analytical infinite-time argument.

originality.rationale: The novelty assessment is confined to the universal phase-dependent nonlinear critical t^{-1} profile and elementary closed amplitude for this concrete deterministic alternating-edge SIS path. The general propagator spectral criterion and the slow-contact advantage are well covered by Speidel et al. 2016 and Valdano et al. 2015/2017, and are not claimed as new; generic inverse-time relaxation elsewhere is also insufficient to imply the phase-resolved vector limit. Relevant source mathematical sections were examined and none inspected stated or directly implied this complete model-specific critical coefficient. This is best-knowledge comparison, not independent certification of world novelty.

The linear threshold is demonstrably covered by broader earlier literature; originality is restricted to the nonlinear phase-resolved coefficient.

scientific_limitations: Deterministic nodewise mean-field SIS, not a finite-state stochastic SIS epidemic.
Explicit critical inverse-time law is restricted to the unique half-period at 1/sqrt(2)<gamma/beta<1.
Does not determine stochastic persistence probability or global answers for general switching graphs.
Unindexed direct specializations of generic periodic epidemic normal forms remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The location of a temporal SIS invasion threshold does not itself quantify how infection clears at the marginal contact duration. The theorem provides a universal phase-resolved critical inverse-time infection profile and an explicit nonlinear coefficient on the smallest connected alternating-two-edge path, a natural exact benchmark for temporal intervention pacing. The complete borderline behavior, rather than a generic spectral computation or arbitrary rational evaluation, is the mathematical value.
